# Fixture Source — Grammar Kernel

## GK-01 Clarity before decoration

- Input condition: A message and supporting proof compete for attention.
- Transformation: Place one short statement before one proof object.
- Intended effect: The user understands the promise before reading detail.
- Evidence IDs: EV-001 EV-104
- Confidence: high
- Alternative explanation: The pattern may exist only for the fixture.
- Exception and scope: Use only inside this synthetic package.
- Protected source expression: Do not copy any real brand expression.
- Acceptance test: One statement clearly precedes proof.
- Rejection test: Decoration becomes the first reading layer.

## GK-02 Separate image jobs

- Input condition: Hero form and detail proof appear together.
- Transformation: Give each image one communication job.
- Intended effect: Product form and evidence remain independently legible.
- Evidence IDs: EV-104 EV-105
- Confidence: high
- Alternative explanation: Separation may be a testing convenience.
- Exception and scope: Use only inside this synthetic package.
- Protected source expression: Keep fixture geometry generic.
- Acceptance test: Every image has one named job.
- Rejection test: One image claims every product benefit.

## GK-03 Reuse modular rhythm

- Input condition: Multiple content types need a shared channel structure.
- Transformation: Reuse the asymmetric module and spacing rhythm.
- Intended effect: Different evidence reads as one system.
- Evidence IDs: EV-102 EV-106
- Confidence: medium
- Alternative explanation: The rhythm may be ordinary grid behavior.
- Exception and scope: Use only inside this synthetic package.
- Protected source expression: Avoid branded motifs.
- Acceptance test: Modules share visible alignment logic.
- Rejection test: Every section invents a new grid.

## GK-04 Make state visible

- Input condition: A product action needs confirmation.
- Transformation: Expose state through a bounded status signal.
- Intended effect: Feedback becomes immediately understandable.
- Evidence IDs: EV-103 EV-108
- Confidence: medium
- Alternative explanation: The status signal may be generic UI practice.
- Exception and scope: Use only inside this synthetic package.
- Protected source expression: Use no proprietary interface pattern.
- Acceptance test: The resulting state is explicit.
- Rejection test: Feedback depends on hidden context.
